results.content: # Effectuation Principles for Career and Innovation in 2026 🚀. During my doctoral research period, I came across Effectuation, a groundbreaking theory developed by Professor Saras Sarasvathy at the University of Virginia’s Darden School of Business to explain how expert entrepreneurs shape the future. What struck me then — and continues to resonate now — is how deeply these principles apply not only to building ventures, but also to shaping our careers. I’ve found these principles equally powerful in guiding career development and innovation management. * Crazy Quilt 🤝 Careers, like ventures, are stitched together through collaborations. 🌍 My own career — spanning innovation ecosystems, international project management, and sustainable transitions — has been deeply influenced by these principles. They remind me that career development, like entrepreneurship, isn’t about predicting the future; it is about creating it. Use what you have, embrace partnerships, take affordable risks, and steer your career with intention.

results.title: Effectuation in action: how pre-commitments drive international ...
results.content: This study examines small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) entrepreneurial internationalization by exploring how effectual decision-making principles and real options reasoning (specifically pre-commitment, staging logic, and affordable loss (influence the creation of foreign market entry opportunities and international performance in 332 New Zealand SMEs. It demonstrates that pre-commitment not only initiates but also drives opportunity creation, which in turn enhances international performance. Effectuation principles, including affordable loss and pre-commitment, balance exploration, and risk management, support opportunity creation, while staging logic reinforces this process by enabling continuous assessment and adaptation (Buccieri et al., 2023. Affordable loss and staging logic mediate the effect of pre-commitment on FME opportunity creation, while experiential learning moderates the link between opportunity creation and international performance. To test the hypothesized mediation effects and the direct relationships among pre-commitment, foreign market entry opportunity creation, and international performance, we followed Gaskin et al. Our findings demonstrate that combining pre-commitment, affordable loss, and staging logic allows SMEs to balance risk and flexibility, enhancing foreign market entry opportunities and international performance.
